spec_match.rationale: Targets the change's headline scenario (touch scrolls no longer light-dismiss) and models it precisely: the instrument distinguishes pointercancel-into-scroll (where even a pair-model engine keeps the popover), completed-pair drags, and taps — matching how the two models actually differ per gesture path.

interactive.rationale: Real scrollable feed with an open popover; every gesture is classified from live pointer/scroll data and the popover's fate is reported per gesture.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises measured-not-asserted verdicts including the pointercancel distinction; matches.

edge_cases.rationale: pointercancel handled explicitly (the first draft missed it — the harness's touch-scroll run produced no verdict because pointerup never fired; fixed and re-verified); taps labelled non-diagnostic-but-correct; gestures with the popover closed labelled non-diagnostic; wheel scrolling honestly excluded in the banner.

references.rationale: Feature index cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/6209615938322432 and the spec PR; the banner explains the flag needs 145+.

conformance.rationale: The suite's popover-machinery and untrusted-immunity assertions underpin the page; trusted-gesture outcomes are demo-measured, not falsely asserted.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141, mobile emulation (360×740 DPR3, touch) via CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent: trusted tap opened the popover; a 6-step touch drag scrolled the feed 135px, fired pointercancel, and the popover SURVIVED — verdict correctly attributes survival to the engine's pointercancel path rather than claiming the click model. Zero console errors; 0px overflow both classes; screenshots read.

design_system.rationale: Feed bordered on paper with stone row separators; verdict rose/emerald; CSS variables only; overscroll-behavior contains the feed.

accessibility.rationale: Feed has aria-label; popover state mirrored in a role=status readout; verdict role=status aria-live; gesture log role=log with labelling heading.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Feed and popover fit narrow viewports (popover max-width 78vw); 0px overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×2000; the touch-only discriminator is stated honestly for desktop.

openQuestions.title: Find a configuration where the legacy scroll-dismissal reproduces
openQuestions.detail: On this engine scrolls escape via pointercancel, so the historical bug (scroll dismissing the popover) was not reproducible here. Test on a real touch device / older Chrome where the pair completed during scroll, and capture the DISMISSED verdict for the archive.

guidanceConsulted.query: overlay over scrollable content touch dismissal
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Contain scroll interactions (overscroll-behavior) and keep overlays predictable during scrolling.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Feed uses overscroll-behavior: contain; the popover's survival across scrolls is the measured subject.

guidanceConsulted.query: popover light dismiss outside click touch scroll gesture
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native popover semantics and observe state via toggle.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All dismissal behavior is native; the page only observes.

summary: Verified headlessly with trusted CDP touch input (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): the harness caught the first draft's missing pointercancel path (touch scrolls produced no verdict), and the fixed instrument now correctly reports this engine's real behavior — scroll survives via pointercancel — without overclaiming the click model.
